Task: ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — ANGLE 2: TESTS & VALIDATION QUALITY (fresh context, read-only).

Target: new uncommitted work in /Users/sofianebebert/workspace/sof-pi: extensions/factory/{index.ts,src/*} plus its test suite tests/factory/{helpers,config,checks,state,rpc,workflow,validator}.test.ts.

Run the tests yourself to see them pass (read-only on the repo):
  cd /Users/sofianebebert/workspace/sof-pi && for f in tests/factory/*.test.ts; do node --experimental-strip-types --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test "$f"; done

Evaluate:
1. Sandbox fidelity: tests/factory/helpers.ts evalWorkflowScript evaluates generated workflow scripts with stubbed runs/state via AsyncFunction. Does that faithfully model the real pi-subagents workflow sandbox semantics (top-level await, return, runs.run/runs.all result shape {runId, structuredOutput, output}, state.set), or could tests pass while the real sandbox diverges? Check against ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-subagents/src/workflows/scripted-workflow.ts.
2. Validator test: tests/factory/validator.test.ts imports the REAL validateWorkflowScript by copying the installed src tree to a temp dir (piSubagentsCopy in helpers.ts). Is that approach sound and deterministic? Any hygiene problems (temp dir reuse, .pnpm skip, cleanup)?
3. RPC smoke test: tests/factory/rpc.test.ts runs the real registerSubagentRpcBridge with a stub execute/context. Are the assertions meaningful (normalization to async:true, invalid_params rejection, correlation, timeout)? Anything important untested (e.g., status method, malformed envelopes, unsubscribe leaks)?
4. Coverage gaps that matter: index.ts (the extension orchestration: git baseline checks, loadConfig, completion handlers, state transitions) has NO tests. Which untested behaviors are risky enough to demand tests now vs acceptable? Which existing tests assert the wrong thing or are tautological?
5. The checks.test.ts real-exec tests use echo/exit/sleep — are they robust cross-platform (macOS/Linux)? Any flakiness?
6. Test ergonomics: node --test + --experimental-strip-types is the runner (no package.json script). Is that acceptable, and is the suite fast/deterministic?

Report ONLY concrete, current, evidence-backed findings with file:line references. P0 = blocks merge (test proves the wrong thing or a real defect escapes). P1 = should fix now. P2 = report-only. End with remainingRisks and a verdict: ok, fix, or blocked.

## Acceptance Contract
Acceptance level: attested
Completion is not accepted from prose alone. End with a structured acceptance report.

Criteria:
- criterion-1: Return concrete findings with file paths and severity when applicable

Required evidence: review-findings, residual-risks

Include an `acceptanceReport` object in your final `structured_output` tool call in this shape:
Use empty arrays when no items apply; array fields contain strings unless object entries are shown.
Empty-string entries (`[""]`) are ignored; use `[]` when nothing applies.
`criteriaSatisfied[].status` must be exactly one of: satisfied, not-satisfied, not-applicable.
`commandsRun[].result` must be exactly one of: passed, failed, not-run.
`manualNotes` and `notes` are optional strings; an empty string means no note and does not satisfy `manual-notes` evidence.
{
  "criteriaSatisfied": [
    {
      "id": "criterion-1",
      "status": "satisfied",
      "evidence": "specific proof"
    }
  ],
  "changedFiles": [
    "src/file.ts"
  ],
  "testsAddedOrUpdated": [
    "test/file.test.ts"
  ],
  "commandsRun": [
    {
      "command": "command",
      "result": "passed",
      "summary": "short result"
    }
  ],
  "validationOutput": [
    "validation output or concise summary"
  ],
  "residualRisks": [
    "none"
  ],
  "noStagedFiles": true,
  "diffSummary": "short description of the diff",
  "reviewFindings": [
    "blocker: file.ts:12 - issue found, or no blockers"
  ],
  "manualNotes": "anything else the parent should know"
}

content.text: I have all the evidence I need. One note: my toolset has no shell/execution tool, so I could not run the test commands myself — the exact commands are reported below for the supervisor to run. I verified all findings by reading the test files, the extension source, the installed `pi-subagents` (v0.61 at `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-subagents`), `package.json`, and `README.md`.

commandsRun.command: for f in tests/factory/*.test.ts; do node --experimental-strip-types --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test "$f"; done
commandsRun.summary: Not run: this reviewer has no shell/exec tool. Supervisor must run the exact command from the task; all other evidence was gathered by reading test files, extension source, package.json, README.md, and the installed pi-subagents v0.61 source.

criteriaSatisfied.evidence: 11 concrete findings (2 P0, 2 P1, 7 P2) with file:line evidence across the factory test suite, extension source, package.json, and installed pi-subagents source; residual risks listed.

acceptanceReport.diffSummary: New uncommitted extension extensions/factory (orchestrator + config/checks/rpc/state/workflow modules) with a 7-file node:test suite (sandboxed workflow evaluation, config/checks/state unit tests, real pi-subagents validator copy, real RPC bridge smoke test, real exec checks).
acceptanceReport.manualNotes: Review scope angle 2 (tests & validation quality). Two P0s are not test-suite bugs per se but are defects the suite structurally cannot catch and they block merge: (1) factory/index.ts is absent from package.json pi.extensions so the extension never loads; (2) generated build workflow launches agent "planner" which does not exist as a builtin or packaged agent. Both were verified against the installed pi-subagents v0.61 source. The P1 'malformed fix handoff → outcome ok' defect is a concrete wrong-transition escape caused precisely by the untested index.ts seam. Sandbox-fidelity answer to Q1: harness diverges from the real VM sandbox (host globals, nested-async rejection, runs.all proxy, JSON return assertion) but currently benign; the real divergence that matters is agent-name resolution, which no test models. Validator copy approach (Q2) is sound and deterministic per-process; main risk is unpinned installed version and non-CI runnability. RPC smoke test (Q3) is meaningful for ping/spawn/correlation/timeout but tests a hand-written script instead of the real generated payloads, and its 'timeout/never reports unknown state as success' test name misdescribes the assertion. Q4: untested-but-risky = completion handlers/correlation (P1 defect found there), restore() round-trip, validateBaseline; acceptable = UI formatting, queryMissionId regex fallback, rpcPing retry. No existing test is tautological enough to flag except the misleading rpc timeout test name and a near-tautological runs.host string check (not flagged). Q5: POSIX-only, low flake risk. Q6: runner acceptable; no package.json test script is the ergonomic gap.
residualRisks: Tests not executed by this reviewer (no exec tool available)
index.ts completion/phase-transition logic remains untested; the P1 outcome=ok defect is likely symptomatic of a broader workflow-verdict vs payload-results divergence
Tests are machine-dependent on ~/.pi/agent installed pi-subagents (unpinned, non-CI)
status-RPC regex parsing and malformed-reply-envelope handling untested
Windows unsupported by real-exec checks tests
reviewFindings: blocker: package.json:12 - factory extension missing from pi.extensions; feature never loads, tests still pass
blocker: extensions/factory/src/workflow.ts:312 - agent "planner" does not exist (not a pi-subagents builtin, not packaged); plan stage fails at runtime
P1: extensions/factory/index.ts:383 - malformed fix handoff (workflow verdict needs_attention) falls through to outcome=ok and reports Factory complete
P1: extensions/factory/index.ts:171 - error message references nonexistent extensions/factory/README.md; README.md also missing the Factory section required by AGENTS.md
P2: tests/factory/helpers.ts:89 - sandbox harness diverges from real VM sandbox (host globals, nested-async rejection, runs.all proxy, JSON return assertion)
P2: tests/factory/rpc.test.ts:89 - smoke test never sends the factory's real generated spawn payload through the real bridge validation
P2: tests/factory/rpc.test.ts:77 - test name misdescribes assertion (req-3 resolves with wrong-shape data instead of timing out)
P2: tests/factory/helpers.ts:119 - validator copy depends on unpinned ~/.pi install and hoisted (non-.pnpm) layout; not CI-runnable
P2: tests/factory/checks.test.ts:51 - real-exec tests POSIX-only; timeout detection tied to literal SIGTERM signal name
P2: tests/factory/rpc.test.ts:150 - dead no-op statement to suppress unused type import
P2: package.json:1 - no test script; runner invocation only documented in task/headers

findings.evidence: package.json:11-15 lists `./extensions/*.ts`, `./extensions/perplexity/index.ts`, `./extensions/background-terminals/index.ts`, `./extensions/learning/index.ts` — no factory entry. extensions/factory/index.ts exists with `export default function factoryExtension(pi: ExtensionAPI)`. Contrast with README.md:35-52, which documents every other extension.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `"./extensions/factory/index.ts"` to the `pi.extensions` array in package.json.
findings.summary: [P0] The factory extension is never loaded: `pi.extensions` in package.json does not include `./extensions/factory/index.ts`. Every other subdirectory extension is explicitly listed; factory is missing, so `/factory` and `/factory-status` never register at runtime. The entire test suite passes while the shipped feature is dead — exactly the 'tests pass, real behavior diverges' failure mode.

findings.evidence: extensions/factory/src/workflow.ts:312 `agent: "planner",` in the build script; pi-subagents src/agents/builtin-names.ts:5-19 (no "planner"); agents/ directory in this repo contains only reviewer.md; no *planner* file under ~/.pi/agent. pi-subagents launch resolution rejects unknown agents (src/agents/agents.ts:318 formatUnknownAgentError).
findings.suggestedFix: Use an existing builtin (e.g. `agent: "scout"` or `agent: "worker"` for planning) or package a `planner` agent under agents/ and list it in package.json `pi.subagents.agents`.
findings.summary: [P0] The plan stage launches `agent: "planner"`, which does not exist: it is not a pi-subagents builtin (builtin-names.ts: advisor, claude-code, codex-exec, delegate, oracle, researcher, reviewer, scout, worker, …) and this package's agents/ dir contains only reviewer.md. At runtime the build workflow fails at the plan stage with "Unknown agent". The test suite cannot catch this: the sandbox harness treats agent names as opaque keys, the validator test only checks script syntax, and the RPC smoke test uses a different hand-written script.

findings.evidence: extensions/factory/index.ts:383 `state.outcome = "ok"; await runFinalChecksAndFinish(...)` is reached whenever `fixHandoff` is undefined and no review verdict is "blocked" — including the case where reviewers requested a fix and the fix worker's handoff was malformed (workflow returned needs_attention). The extension never inspects the workflow-level return verdict; it recomputes disposition solely from `payload.results` (index.ts:360-383).
findings.suggestedFix: Distinguish 'no fix was needed' from 'fix ran and produced no valid handoff': e.g. check whether any review verdict was "fix" when fixHandoff is undefined and route that case to needs_attention instead of outcome=ok.
findings.summary: [P1] A malformed fix-worker handoff makes the factory report SUCCESS: the review workflow script fails closed with verdict needs_attention (workflow.ts:415), but handleReviewCompletion ignores the workflow return verdict and, with one reviewer verdict=fix and no blocked verdicts, falls through to `state.outcome = "ok"` and runs final checks — the user sees 'Factory complete' after a fix pass that produced no valid acceptance handoff. This violates the fail-closed contract stated in workflow.ts:18 and is untested because index.ts has zero tests.

findings.evidence: AGENTS.md requires README updates 'as part of the same change set'. README.md Extensions section (README.md:35-52) covers perplexity, background-terminals, learning only. index.ts:170-171: `See extensions/factory/README.md for the schema.`; `ls extensions/factory` shows only index.ts and src/.
findings.suggestedFix: Write extensions/factory/README.md documenting the .pi/factory.json schema, add a Factory section to README.md, and commit both with the change.
findings.summary: [P1] Project-standard doc sync is missing AND a broken doc pointer ships in an error message: AGENTS.md requires the README to be updated in the same change set when adding an extension, but README.md has no Factory section; additionally index.ts:171 tells users to 'See extensions/factory/README.md for the schema' and that file does not exist.

findings.evidence: helpers.ts:89-91 builds the script body via AsyncFunction; real sandbox uses vm.createContext with a restricted globals object plus the workflowPromise proxy (scripted-workflow.ts:884-886) and rejects nested async helpers via assertPortableWorkflowScript (scripted-workflow.ts:765-793, NESTED_ASYNC_WORKFLOW_ERROR).
findings.suggestedFix: Optionally run generated scripts once through the real worker validate path (assertPortableWorkflowScript is already covered by the validator test) and consider asserting the script source contains no `process.`/`require(`/`import(` tokens.
findings.summary: [P2] Sandbox harness is not the real sandbox — three divergences let tests pass on scripts the real sandbox would reject: (1) the harness evaluates via AsyncFunction in the test process's global scope, so scripts can reference host globals (process, dynamic import) that the real VM context blocks; (2) nested async functions are allowed by the harness but rejected by the real sandbox (NESTED_ASYNC_WORKFLOW_ERROR); (3) the harness's runs.all returns a plain array while the real one returns a Proxy that throws on non-index property access, and the real return-value JSON assertion (assertJsonValue, undefined→null) is not modeled. Currently benign (generated scripts use only top-level await, plain functions, index access, plain-JSON returns), and the nested-async rule is partially covered statically by validator.test.ts via real validateWorkflowScript.

findings.evidence: rpc.test.ts:89-93 `workflowScript: 'const scout = await runs.run("scout", { agent: "scout", task: "t" }); return scout.structuredOutput;'` while the real requests are built by buildBuildWorkflowScript/buildReviewWorkflowScript with agent/context/outputSchema/acceptance fields (workflow.ts:296-336, 404-410).
findings.suggestedFix: Import buildBuildWorkflowScript and send its output (plus mission/timeoutMs/globalConcurrencyLimit exactly as spawnWorkflow does) through the real bridge in the smoke test; assert invalid_params is not raised.
findings.summary: [P2] The RPC smoke test validates a hand-written minimal workflowScript, never the factory's actual generated spawn payloads. The real spawn boundary (rpc.ts spawnParams → normalizePublicSubagentExecution, rpc.ts:512-520) never sees the factory's real param shape, so a schema-level rejection of the real payload (e.g. mission shape, timeoutMs bounds, outputSchema/acceptance interaction) would escape all tests.

findings.evidence: rpc.test.ts:77-85: name says timeout/no-success-on-unknown-state, but req-3 resolves successfully and `await pending` passes; the only timeout assertion is on req-4 (rpc.test.ts:82-83).
findings.suggestedFix: Rename to describe actual behavior (wrong-shape success reply resolves; second request times out), or add reply-envelope shape validation to rpcRequest and assert the wrong-shape reply times out.
findings.summary: [P2] Test name misrepresents what is asserted: 'times out when no correlated reply arrives — never reports unknown state as success' actually emits a correlated success reply for req-3 with wrong-shaped data and the promise RESOLVES (`await pending` at rpc.test.ts:85). The rpc client performs no reply shape validation, so this documents the opposite of the name; the real timeout path is only exercised by req-4.

findings.evidence: helpers.ts:113-140: mkdtempSync temp copy, cpSync of src, symlink of node_modules skipping .pnpm, process 'exit' cleanup; validator.test.ts:22-30 imports from the copy. PI_SUBAGENTS_PATH override exists (helpers.ts:114-116) but nothing pins/records the version under test.
findings.suggestedFix: Acceptable for a personal-machine setup; consider reading and asserting the installed package version (or recording it in output) so drift is visible, and document PI_SUBAGENTS_PATH for other machines.
findings.summary: [P2] Validator/RPC approach is sound per-run but machine- and version-dependent: piSubagentsCopy copies ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-subagents (or PI_SUBAGENTS_PATH) into a fresh mkdtemp per process with best-effort exit cleanup and skips .pnpm, relying on hoisted deps at ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules. Temp-dir hygiene is fine (unique dir per process, rmSync on exit, rejected-copy cached and fails loudly), but the installed pi-subagents version is unpinned — a pi update can silently change validation/RPC semantics the tests encode. Also non-runnable in CI without the install.

findings.evidence: checks.test.ts:51-62 uses runner("echo hello"/"exit 3"/"sleep 5", …); checks.ts:44-46 `timedOut = error.killed && error.signal === "SIGTERM"`.
findings.suggestedFix: No change needed for this repo; optionally note POSIX-only in a comment, or derive timedOut from `error.killed` alone to be robust across kill signals.
findings.summary: [P2] Real-exec check tests are POSIX-only and tie timeout detection to a literal signal name: `echo`/`exit 3`/`sleep 5` work on macOS/Linux but not Windows cmd; and createExecCheckRunner's timedOut requires `signal === "SIGTERM"` (checks.ts:44-47), which holds for Node's default exec killSignal but breaks if killSignal is ever changed. Timing flake risk is low (300ms budget against `sleep 5`); note exec kills the shell, leaving `sleep` orphaned briefly — harmless.

findings.evidence: rpc.test.ts:150 `void (null as unknown as SandboxStubChild);` — no behavior, exists to consume the type import at rpc.test.ts:3.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete line 150 and the `type SandboxStubChild` import.
findings.summary: [P2] Dead test code: `void (null as unknown as SandboxStubChild);` at the end of the smoke test is a no-op whose only purpose is to suppress an unused type import; the SandboxStubChild import in rpc.test.ts is otherwise unused.

findings.evidence: package.json has no scripts section (whole file read); runner is documented in the task and tests/factory/helpers.ts header. Most tests are deterministic; only checks.test.ts (300ms timeout) and rpc.test.ts (30-50ms timeouts) use wall-clock timing, with generous margins.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a `test` script (e.g. `node --experimental-strip-types --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test tests/factory/*.test.ts`) so the invocation is canonical and discoverable.
findings.summary: [P2] Test ergonomics: there is no `test` script in package.json at all; the suite only runs via the documented `node --experimental-strip-types --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test <file>` loop, which requires Node ≥22.6 and is easy to run wrong. Runner choice itself is acceptable for a personal pi package with no build step.

remainingRisks: Test suite was NOT executed (review tooling has no shell); pass/fail of the seven factory test files is unattested and the supervisor should run the documented node --test loop before merge.

index.ts completion correlation, phase transitions, restore()/save() session round-trip, validateBaseline git gating, and rpcPing's 1s retry path remain untested; the P1 outcome=ok defect is one instance of what is likely a broader gap between workflow-script return verdicts and the extension's recomputed disposition (the extension never reads the workflow's returned `verdict`).

status RPC surface (queryMissionId/factory-status regexes `/Mission:\s+(\S+)/` and `/State:\s+(\S+)/` against the real bridge's status text) is untested; format drift degrades silently to undefined, which is graceful but means mission ids may never populate.
Tests depend on the developer's installed pi-subagents at ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules (unpinned version, non-CI-runnable); a pi update can silently change the semantics the tests encode.
Malformed RPC reply envelopes (non-object payloads, missing error object) are handled by rpc.ts but untested.
Windows is unsupported by the real-exec checks tests and likely by the whole extension (git/shell assumptions); presumably acceptable for this personal package.
